analysis.summary: Kubernetes v1.36.0-beta.0 是一个以稳定性和性能优化为主的版本，包含多项功能毕业（GA/Beta）、重要 Bug 修复、内存泄漏修复以及一个需要立即关注的监控指标变更。
key_changes: 紧急变更：kube-controller-manager 指标 `volume_operation_total_errors` 重命名为 `volume_operation_errors_total` - [PR #136399](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136399) - **影响：** 所有使用此指标的自定义监控仪表板或告警规则必须更新。
API 废弃：开始废弃 `Service.spec.externalIPs` 字段，未来版本将移除 - [PR #137293](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137293) - **影响：** 使用此字段的服务将收到警告，需规划迁移至 LoadBalancer 或 Ingress。
功能毕业：动态资源分配（DRA）扩展资源功能升级至 Beta - [PR #135048](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135048) - **影响：** 为设备管理（如 GPU、FPGA）提供了更稳定的 API。
功能毕业：节点声明功能（NodeDeclaredFeatures）升级至 Beta，作为多个功能（如原地垂直伸缩、WebSocket 直连）的基础 - [PR #136042](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136042)
新功能：HPA 支持基于条件的缩放到零（Alpha） - [PR #135118](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135118) - **影响：** 允许根据自定义条件将副本数缩至零，节省资源。
API 变更：废弃直接访问 `fieldsV1.Raw` 字段，推荐使用封装访问器 - [PR #137304](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137304) - **影响：** 使用 Server-Side Apply 并直接操作 Raw 字段的客户端库需要更新。
important_bugfixes: 修复 client-go 在集群 CA 轮换时无法重新加载信任根证书的问题 - [PR #132922](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/132922) - **影响：** 修复了 CA 轮换期间客户端连接永久中断的关键问题，需关注升级。
修复 client-go TLS 缓存内存泄漏问题，添加自动垃圾回收 - [PR #136355](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136355) - **影响：** 解决长期运行进程连接多个集群时的内存持续增长问题。
修复垃圾收集器（GC）在外部删除对象后记录大量 NotFound 错误日志的问题 - [PR #136817](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136817) - **影响：** 减少控制平面日志噪音，提升可观测性。
修复高核数机器上 nf_conntrack 限制计算过高导致内存过度消耗的问题 - [PR #137002](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137002) - **影响：** 防止拥有大量 CPU 核心的节点因网络配置消耗过多内存。
修复 `kubelet_pod_start_sli_duration_seconds` 指标未正确排除初始化容器运行时间的问题 - [PR #131950](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/131950) - **影响：** 使 Pod 启动 SLI 指标更准确，影响 SLO 监控。
修复 `kubectl attach` 命令不支持 `--detach-keys` 参数的问题 - [PR #134997](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134997) - **影响：** 提升运维人员使用体验。
security_issues: 修复 client-go CA 证书重载问题，提升 CA 轮换安全性 - [PR #132922](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/132922) - **风险级别：** 中
修复 client-go TLS 缓存内存泄漏，无直接安全风险但影响稳定性 - [PR #136355](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136355) - **风险级别：** 低
performance_improvements: 优化：`kubectl describe` 在描述多个对象时默认跳过查询事件，大幅减少 API 调用 - [PR #137145](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137145) - **提升：** 描述含 500 个 Pod 的命名空间可减少 500 次 API 调用。
优化：DRA 资源切片控制器引入基于索引的命名和字典序排序，提升调度器选择设备的可预测性和性能 - [PR #136641](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136641)
优化：为原地 Pod 垂直伸缩创建准入插件，在 API 层提前进行节点容量和 OS 检查，避免无效请求下发到 kubelet - [PR #136043](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136043) - **提升：** 失败更快，减少不必要的工作负载。
breaking_changes: 破坏性变更：kube-controller-manager 指标重命名 `volume_operation_total_errors` -> `volume_operation_errors_total` - [PR #136399](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136399) - **影响：** 必须更新所有相关的监控仪表板、告警规则和自动化脚本。
API 变更：将 kuberc 凭证插件白名单条目的 `name` 字段重命名为 `command` 以与 kubeconfig 保持一致 - [PR #137272](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137272) - **影响：** 使用此 Beta API 的配置文件需要更新字段名。
recommendations: **立即行动：** 检查并更新所有监控系统中引用的 `volume_operation_total_errors` 指标，改为 `volume_operation_errors_total`。
**规划迁移：** 评估集群中是否使用 `Service.spec.externalIPs`，并开始规划迁移至 LoadBalancer 或 Ingress 控制器。
**测试重点：** 在测试环境中重点验证 client-go CA 重载修复（PR #132922）和 TLS 缓存 GC（PR #136355），特别是涉及多集群连接和证书轮换的场景。
**升级前检查：** 如果使用 Server-Side Apply 并直接操作 `fieldsV1.Raw`，确认客户端库已适配新的访问器接口。
**性能评估：** 在高核数节点上验证 nf_conntrack 内存使用是否恢复正常。
**利用新功能：** 考虑试用 HPA 基于条件的缩放到零功能，以优化资源成本。
analysis.risk_assessment: 整体风险评估：**中等**。此版本包含一个必须处理的紧急指标变更（ACTION REQUIRED）和一个重要的 API 废弃开端。同时，修复了 CA 轮换和内存泄漏等关键稳定性问题。建议在非生产环境充分测试后，规划升级。需要特别关注监控系统的兼容性更新和 `Service.spec.externalIPs` 的迁移准备。对于大规模集群，PR #137145 的性能优化将带来显著收益。

137304.title: refactor: fieldsv1 encapsulation via accessors and deprecation of direct "Raw" field usage
137304.body:
<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request!  Here are some tips for you:

1. If this is your first time, please read our contributor guidelines: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/first-contribution.md#your-first-contribution and developer guide https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/development.md#development-guide
2. Please label this pull request according to what type of issue you are addressing, especially if this is a release targeted pull request. For reference on required PR/issue labels, read here:
https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-release/release.md#issuepr-kind-label
3. Ensure you have added or ran the appropriate tests for your PR: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-testing/testing.md
4. If you want *faster* PR reviews, read how: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/pull-requests.md#best-practices-for-faster-reviews
5. If the PR is unfinished, see how to mark it: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/pull-requests.md#marking-unfinished-pull-requests
-->

#### What type of PR is this?
/kind cleanup
/kind api-change
/kind deprecation

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
This PR attempts to encapsulate `FieldsV1` access to prepare for interning memory optimizations.

Currently, `metav1.FieldsV1` exposes the underlying payload directly via the `.Raw` `[]byte` slice. The goal of the PR is to make it so all k/k accesses to `metav1.FieldsV1` are done through accessor methods in a first step towards interning of FieldsV1 values.

This PR:
1.  Moves `FieldsV1` and its generated protobuf/deepcopy logic into a standalone file (`fieldsv1_byte.go`).
2.  Marks the `Raw` field as deprecated.
3.  Implements "overload" getters and setters for different formats (`GetRawBytes`, `GetRawString`, `GetRawReader`).
4.  Updates all in-tree call sites to use the new accessors.
5. Updates the MarshallJSON and MarshalCBOR logic to do a `len(raw) == 0`  check from previously a `f.Raw == nil` check to set the []byte("null"}).  This is a small behaviour change where an empty []byte{} goes from previously erroring on CREATE to now being set to to []byte("null") but in practice an empty []byte{} being marshalled does not occur as the field is omitempty.  This change is done to better handle the []byte{} case as well as to setup for potential future where FieldsV1.Raw can be toggled to be a string (where we want len check)

**Performance Note:** We explicitly implemented format-specific accessors here. Because the underlying field is a `[]byte` today, this allows hot-path components (like JSON, CBOR, and Protobuf deserializers) to utilize `SetRawBytes` and `GetRawBytes` so performance is not impacted

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/137109


#### Special notes for your reviewer:
This PR builds upon an initial PoC by @liggitt  here - https://github.com/liggitt/kubernetes/commits/fieldsv1-string/ only this PR updates the accessor strategy to "overload" accessors and thus not having any type conversions.  This is done to ensure no performance regressions can be introduced to the master branch during this refactor.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
Direct access to the `Raw` field of `metav1.FieldsV1` is deprecated. Code that constructs or reads `FieldsV1` should migrate to the new `NewFieldsV1(string)`, `GetRawBytes()`, `GetRawString()`, and `SetRawBytes()` accessor methods.
```

```docs
```

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
PodStartSLIDuration does not behave according to documentation: https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/sig-scalability/slos/pod_startup_latency.md
It should exclude init container runtime and image pulling time, and include only stateless and immediately schedulable pods.

#### How this was tested:
```bash
kind create cluster --name $CLUSTER_NAME
# rebuilt kubelet for Linux because kind runs linux containers
GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go build -o _output/kubelet ./cmd/kubelet
# deploy custom kubelet to node
docker cp _output/kubelet ${CLUSTER_NAME}-control-plane:/usr/bin/kubelet
docker exec ${CLUSTER_NAME}-control-plane systemctl restart kubelet
kubectl apply -f stateless-stateful-test.yaml
# get metrics once pods are all running
kubectl get --raw="/api/v1/nodes/${CLUSTER_NAME}-control-plane/proxy/metrics" | grep "kubelet_pod_start_sli_duration_seconds"
```
If you want to test another deployment and reset metrics:
```bash
kubectl delete deployment stateless-test stateful-test
#reset metrics by restarting kubelet
docker exec ${CLUSTER_NAME}-control-plane systemctl restart kubelet
kubectl apply -f init-container-test.yaml
# get metrics once pods are all running
kubectl get --raw="/api/v1/nodes/${CLUSTER_NAME}-control-plane/proxy/metrics" | grep "kubelet_pod_start_sli_duration_seconds"
```

Tested this with 5 stateless and 10 stateful pods with the `stateless-stateful-test.yaml` deployment like:
```yaml
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: test-pvc
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: stateless-test
  labels:
    app: stateless-test
spec:
  replicas: 5
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: stateless-test
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: stateless-test
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: init-container
```

136817.title: Handle NotFound errors in garbage collector
136817.body:
## What type of PR is this?
/kind bug

## What this PR does / why we need it:

This PR fixes issue #136525 where the Garbage Collector logs spurious error messages when attempting to delete objects that have already been deleted externally.

In scenarios where users delete pods directly after deleting jobs (to free up resources faster), the GC later attempts to delete these already-deleted pods, resulting in NotFound errors being logged as errors.

## How does this PR address the issue?

The fix adds explicit NotFound error handling in the `attemptToDeleteItem` function after `deleteObject` calls. When a NotFound error occurs:

1. A virtual delete event is enqueued via `gc.dependencyGraphBuilder.enqueueVirtualDeleteEvent(item.identity)`
2. Return `enqueuedVirtualDeleteEventErr`

This approach is consistent with the existing behavior when `getObject` returns NotFound (lines 523-531), ensuring uniform handling throughout the function.

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #136525

## Special notes for your reviewer:

The changes are minimal and follow the existing pattern in the codebase. The fix only affects two locations where `deleteObject` is called (lines 628 and 649 in the original code).

## Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
Garbage collector now correctly handles objects deleted externally, preventing spurious error logs.
```

136256.title: Extend WebSocket Streaming Protocol to the Kubelet for Exec/Attach/PortForward
136256.body:
**Extend WebSocket Streaming Protocol to the Kubelet for Exec/Attach/PortForward**

* When `ExtendWebSocketsToKubelet` is enabled and a `kubelet` node advertises support, `exec/attach/portforward` streams are proxied directly to the `kubelet` rather than being translated or tunneled at the API server. Critically, the same stream translation and tunneling handlers used at the API server are now set up identically at the `kubelet` — the logic is simply moved closer to the container runtime. This feature depends on `NodeDeclaredFeatures` graduating to beta so that `kubelet` capability advertisement is reliable in production clusters.

* This PR adds two new ALPHA metrics: `apiserver_websocket_streaming_requests_total{subresource, proxy_type}` is incremented at routing decision time in the API server's `Connect()` handlers, with `proxy_type` set to `proxied_to_kubelet`, `translated_at_apiserver`, or `tunneled_at_apiserver` depending on feature gate state and node capability. `kubelet_streaming_websocket_requests_total{subresource}` is incremented at the `kubelet` when an actual WebSocket session arrives with the stream-close or tunneling protocol, giving a node-level view of WebSocket traffic volume.

* Unit tests cover both new metrics directly, and metric assertions are added to the existing `TestExecRESTConnect`, `TestAttachRESTConnect`, and `TestPortForwardRESTConnect` table tests in `subresources_test.go`, verifying the correct `proxy_type` label is emitted for each routing scenario.

/kind feature

```release-note
Adds the ExtendWebSocketsToKubelet feature gate (Beta, default true in v1.36). When enabled, the API server proxies WebSocket exec/attach/portforward requests directly to the kubelet rather than translating or tunneling them at the API server. The kubelet now handles WebSocket-to-SPDY stream translation (exec/attach) and WebSocket tunneling (portforward) using the same handlers previously used at the API server. The kubelet advertises support for this feature to the API server via the NodeDeclaredFeatures mechanism; the API server only proxies directly to a kubelet that has advertised support. Two new ALPHA metrics are added to track routing decisions and WebSocket streaming volume: apiserver_websocket_streaming_requests_total (labels: subresource, proxy_type) and kubelet_streaming_websocket_requests_total (label: subresource).
```

136641.title: DRA: Introduce index-based naming in resourceslice controller and sort slices and pools lexicographically
136641.body:
#### What type of PR is this?
/kind feature

#### What this PR does / why we need it:
https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/5794 discussed setting priority for `ResourceSlices` and `Pools`. We eventually agreed to sort slices and pools in lexicographical order to avoid API changes. Below is a summary of the changes and relevant notes.

**Allocator**
When gathering pools, we now sort slices and pools by name. Since the allocator uses a first-fit search, this allows driver authors to influence prioritization through their naming conventions. Notably, we no longer treat slices with binding conditions specially, as driver authors now have the flexibility to control the order themselves. Since different pools may be published by different drivers, we'll still consider pools without binding conditions first as we do currently.

**Resource Slice Controller**
Prior to this PR, slices were named randomly and matched with existing slices based on their content. This PR introduces index-based naming, where slices are named in the order provided by the driver. Consequently, the allocation process considers slices in the driver-specified order. Also, slices are now matched by names in synchronization.

While inserting a new slice requires updating all subsequent slices, this does not result in a performance degradation. Previously, adding a new slice required bumping the generation, which also necessitated updating all slices.

When users upgrade from an older version to this one, existing slices will be recreated with index-based names. This behavior is covered in the included unit tests.

**Test**
Since the new allocation feature is currently exclusive to the experimental allocator and not behind a feature gate, I have placed the related tests in a separate section named after the feature. I anticipate these may be referenced by multiple channels in the future; for example, if the feature moves from experimental to incubating, these lexicographical tests can be shared across both channels.

#### Which issue(s) this PR is related to:
Fixes #136628

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?
```release-note
Introduce index-based naming in ResourceSlice controller and ensure ResourceSlices and pools are sorted lexicographically before allocation, allowing users to control allocation priority.
```

137109.body:
### What would you like to be added? I propose implementing object interning (deduplication) techniques in the Kubernetes API Server and control plane components to significantly reduce memory usage. Specifically, this proposal suggests: * **String Interning:** Modifying protobuf deserialization to intern strings during decoding. [PoC](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/c8ff1377dcebe18effe75166507bf624afbe008e) * **ManagedFields Deduplication:** Implementing custom deserialization for FieldsV1 (Server-Side Apply metadata) to reuse existing objects. [PoC](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/627898045327206f37b347c65ba84d0fdb69b361) * **JSON Optimization:** Evaluating a migration to json/v2 for built-in interning support. Work related to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/134375 ### Why is this needed? As Kubernetes adoption grows, particularly with the rise of AI/ML workloads, cluster scales are pushing beyond traditional limits. * **High Replication & Redundancy:** We are increasingly seeing Jobs, Deployments, and StatefulSets scaling to 10,000+ replicas. In these highly replicated workloads, the PodSpec is largely identical across replicas, leading to massive redundancy in memory. Etcd already started getting feature request to handle it better [etcd-io/etcd#21305](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/issues/21305), * **Memory Bottlenecks:** The API server consumes approximately 10x the raw resource size in memory to maintaining latest state and history in watch cache and latest state in informer. With the increase in replication and resource complexity, memory overhead becomes the primary limiting factor for horizontal scaling. * **ManagedFields Overhead:** By design, Server-Side Apply (SSA) metadata accounts for >50% of the stored resource size[KEP-555](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-api-machinery/555-server-side-apply#scalability). Initial implementations caused API server crashes due to concurrent map writes, and while deep-copying mitigated this, the approach remains fragile due to hidden mutations (e.g., defaulting, admission). * **Dropping unused Informer fields:** We considered dropping unused fields from the API Server's internal informers. 135341.title: [InPlacePodVerticalScaling] Move feasibility checks to admission
135341.body:
This is an umbrella issue to track the work of moving feasibility checks to admission.

Resizes can be considered infeasible for the following reasons:
- The requested resources exceed the node's total capacity.
- The pod is running on a node with an OS that does not support resize (like windows).
- The pod is a static pod.
- The feature gate is disabled on the node.
- Resize is not supported in combination with a few other features, which are:
  - Swap
  - Static CPU manager
  - Static memory manager


For infeasible resizes, the admission controller accepts the resize patch, with the feasibility check subsequently performed by the kubelet prior to resource allocation. If the resize is deemed infeasible, the kubelet adds a PodResizePending / Infeasible condition to the pod. An optimization we can make is to instead move these feasibility checks to admission, instead of accepting the patch and waiting for the kubelet to reject the resize.

The first 3 are trivial to move to admission. The remaining ones can be handled using the node declared features framework once we have commitment to implement those features so that we have a feature gate that we can tie the NDFs to.

/cc @tallclair @pravk03 
/assign

119483.title: client-go doesn't properly handle reloading trust anchors during cluster CA rotation
119483.body:
Discussed in SIG Auth: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1woLGRoONE3EBVx-wTb4pvp4CI7tmLZ6lS26VTbosLKM/edit#bookmark=id.5mfr9vowfkwr

The kube-apiserver serving root CA certificate is injected into pods at /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt.

Client-go reads it once [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/6c596fdbc11ce7779ee320c6a11df44c5d516d54/rest/config.go#L528).  Normally the transport is supposed to automatically reload the roots, but it doesn't set reloadTLSFiles if a CAFile is set [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/928adb27abf755b402be7594844e3c248b0b7670/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/transport/transport.go#L155-L168).

The net effect is that most clients using InClusterConfig will find their connection to kube-apiserver permanently broken during a rotation of the kube-apiserver serving CA, and won't recover until they are restarted.

We should:
* Set reloadTLSFiles when CAFile is set.
* Make sure that reloadTLSFiles will actually re-read the CAFile.
* Add a test.

Reason for the leak:
We're using `kubernetes.NewForConfig` which eventually calls `transport.New(config)`
That transport calls `tlsCache.get`: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/3b5044fefd5a9a192b379236fac11ac8c41a7017/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/transport/transport.go#L50

`tlsCache` is a non-exported global that implements a http transport cache. The `get` also stores the given transport in the cache if it's not there, yet.
However there are no mechanisms that would remove something from the cache. Neither explicitly, nor through expiration or anything.
The cache key includes k8s cert data which means every cluster we connect to will create a new cache entry that will then stay there indefinitely.

135329.title: [NodeDeclaredFeatures] GuaranteedQoSPodCPUResize version skew problem
135329.body:
The `GuaranteedQoSPodCPUResize` node declared feature isn't just tied to the `InPlacePodVerticalScalingExclusiveCPUs` feature gate: it declares the feature if the feature gate is enabled OR the node doesn't use static CPU policy, and then requires the feature gate for all CPU resizes of guaranteed pods.

Here is the problem:
- v1.34 node: in-place pod resize is enabled, static policy disabled
	- 1.34 is pre-NDF, so it doesn't declare any features
- v1.35 control plane: NDF disabled (still alpha)
	- resizing guaranteed pod CPU is allowed (no NDF admission check), node doesn't mark resize as infeasible since it doesn't have static CPU policy.
- Upgrade cluster to v1.36: NDF goes beta & default enabled
	- Now resizing a guaranteed pod's CPU requires the `GuaranteedQoSPodCPUResize`, but the v1.34 node still doesn't set it, causing a regression.

I don't think we need to fix this in v1.35 since NDF is still alpha, but this is a beta-blocker.

136228.title: kubernetes is reconfiguring iptables/netfilter data structures with bad settings
136228.body:
### What happened?

Hello,

I've been debugging issues with my Kubernetes nodes having very high CPU usage in network components.

I've finally traced down the origin to that block of code, which is overriding sysctl settings for iptables with insanely high values.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/proxy/conntrack/sysctls.go#L62

The default is for the kernel to configurable iptables data structures based on available memory. Typically 32k-256k buckets and 256k max entries (this may be a tad low for the most busy servers). 

**Problem: Kubernetes is reconfiguring the iptables data structures based on the number of CPU cores. It's broken on machines with many CPU.
On my servers with 512 cores, I am seeing Kubernetes reconfigure the kernel to have 16M iptables entries with a 4M hash table.
That's a 32 MB hash table that can't fit in CPU cache, with 6 GB of entries. It's ridiculous.**

The large data structure is causing constant thrashing of the CPU cache on all cores, as every network packet has to lookup the table multiple times, and network packets are distributed across all CPU cores for processing.

Some operations need to go over the whole hashtable, for read or write (write has locks), which is affected by the large size of the table. This is why you've been having issues with nginx proxy (among other bugs), you've got bug tickets investigating performance issue with processing/updating that table, but nobody pointing out that it should not have millions of items, no wonder it's slow to process!

Can you please correct this code?

This should be set to a fixed value. I think 256k buckets, 1M max entries is a good default value that should work for >99% of users.
If anyone reaches that limit, they should check with `netstat` what is consuming active entries, then they probably need to reduce the sysctl timeout to evict these entries faster, as the default is keeping them for too long.

```
net.nf_conntrack_max = 1048576
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_buckets = 262144
```

Regards.

iptables should have reasonable configuration

136631.title: setcap build image shouldn't require a shell
136631.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Building with a more vanilla setcap image shouldn't require a shell in the image to run the command 


in `build/server-image/kube-apiserver/Dockerfile`

```sh
# We apply cap_net_bind_service so that kube-apiserver can be run as
# non-root and still listen on port less than 1024
RUN setcap cap_net_bind_service=+ep /${BINARY}
```

this command requires the `SETCAP_IMAGE` have a shell in order to:
1) RUN a command that isn't in the form of ["/usr/sbin/setcap", "..."] 
2) shell expand the `${BINARY}` argument


### Why is this needed?

By making this change you can eliminate the need of having a shell in the setcap image:


```diff
diff --git a/build/server-image/kube-apiserver/Dockerfile b/build/server-image/kube-apiserver/Dockerfile
index 27129d29bd9..acfe8c26f22 100644
--- a/build/server-image/kube-apiserver/Dockerfile
+++ b/build/server-image/kube-apiserver/Dockerfile
@@ -20,11 +20,11 @@ ARG SETCAP_IMAGE
 # to setup qemu for the builder.
 FROM --platform=linux/$BUILDARCH ${SETCAP_IMAGE}
 ARG BINARY
-COPY --chmod=755 ${BINARY} /${BINARY}
+COPY --chmod=755 ${BINARY} /set_cap_binary
 # We apply cap_net_bind_service so that kube-apiserver can be run as
 # non-root and still listen on port less than 1024
-RUN setcap cap_net_bind_service=+ep /${BINARY}
+RUN ["setcap", "cap_net_bind_service=+ep", "/set_cap_binary"]
 
 FROM --platform=linux/$TARGETARCH ${BASEIMAGE}
 ARG BINARY
-COPY --from=0 /${BINARY} /usr/local/bin/${BINARY}
+COPY --from=0 /set_cap_binary /usr/local/bin/${BINARY}
```

136628.title: Let DRA drivers specify the order in which devices are considered during scheduling
136628.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Currently the order in which the DRA allocator considers devices during scheduling is non-deterministic. Since the DRA allocator uses a first-fit algorithm, the order in which devices are considered can impact both the time required to schedule pods and which devices are selected.

We want to let DRA drivers specify the order in which the allocator will consider devices. This is discussed in more detail in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5773 and https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/5794.

### Why is this needed?

This will allow faster scheduling and allocation of more appropriate devices.
